text:
lauren: quick sync — we need to decide how saved views behave when users pin per-route vs per-model defaults. do we persist a single view with a scope flag or keep separate objects?
raj: my vote: single object + `scope` enum. avoids dupes in DB and makes rollbacks easier.
tessa: worried about UX — if a user pins model-scoped view but route has its own pinned view, which wins? need deterministic precedence.
oren: precedence idea: route > model > org. route-scoped view only applies when route has explicit values, otherwise fall back. simple and predictable.
lauren: that precedence works. also need to surface cost + telemetry sampling differences in the UI. saved view should show an estimated token burn and sample rate.
raj: agree. for API shape I'm proposing:
```
POST /api/console/saved_views
{
  "name": "Errors + latency (p99)",
  "filters": {"route": "graphql\/user", "model": "redwood/gpt-embed-4"},
  "scope": "route", // route | model | org
  "cost_preview": true,
  "telemetry": {"sampling_rate": 0.01}
}
```
lauren: tl;dr: scope enum + telemetry + cost_preview flags. two debates left: default sampling behavior for saved queries, and backward compat for old views (no scope field).
tessa: default sampling: inherit workspace-level sampling unless user explicitly sets sampling in view. otherwise we risk over-indexing on low-traffic views.
raj: for backward compat, fall back to `org` scope when missing, but mark migrated views and surface a migration prompt in console.
oren: also need to think about routing policy impacts: if a saved view references a routed model variant (e.g., cheaper fallback), cost_preview should compute both nominal and fallback costs. UI should show "expected" vs "worst-case".
lauren: good catch. UX sketch: show two columns in preview: nominal (route->primary) and fallback (route->fallbacks). also a little ? tooltip: "preview assumes current routing policy; costs change if policy changes".
raj: implementation note — the existing fetch endpoint is `/v1/console/views/:id` and returns `filters` + `query`. we'll need to add `scope`, `telemetry` and `cost_preview` fields and keep old keys. propose soft rollout behind `console.savedViews.v2` flag.
lauren: can deploy behind flag. @deploy-bot can you confirm flag exists in prod targeting 50%?
deploy-bot: featureflag `console.savedViews.v2` currently OFF in prod. toggles available via /internal/flags. (rancheck 1764019900)
tessa: for rollout plan: enable flag for internal orgs + staging, migrate 10% of customer views, run telemetry checks for sampling drift. if drift > 2% trigger rollback.
lauren: what metrics do we track during canary?
raj: track: saved_views.fetch latency, cost_preview compute time, telemetry events per-view (sampled vs unsampled), and mismatch rate where user's expected sampling != actual.
oren: also add an alert if cost_preview errors spike (which happened last time when routing graph changed).
lauren: final Q: should saved view editing preserve previous versions? i think yes — keep `versions` array and let rollback via UI.
tessa: don't store huge payloads inline. keep pointers to snapshots. we can keep a small metadata `versions` list.
lauren: ok. action items:
- raj: draft API change + migration script (PR this week)
- oren: wire up cost_preview to include routing fallback logic + unit tests
- tessa: add UX mock for preview columns + migration prompt copy
- lauren: rollout plan doc and gate criteria

lauren: ping me here when PRs land, will sync with infra to open flipper for 10% canary.
raj: on it. will include example fallback-cost calculation and a sample of migrated payloads.
lauren: thanks all :raised_hands:
